The app helps you quickly generate standardized Cutter numbers for your library\'s call numbers. Simply search for an author\'s name or book title, and Cutter App will instantly match it to the correct entry.
Go to the %1$s tab, tap the top menu (•••), and choose %2$s to select which table the app should use for matches.
How do I change the active Cutter table?
Which articles (grammar) can be ignored by the app?
You can configure call numbers to ignore grammatical articles. For example, "The King in Yellow" is treated as "King in Yellow". The following articles can be automatically ignored:
Can I look up books by scanning a barcode?

Yes! You can point your device’s camera at any book\'s barcode (EAN-13 or EAN-8) to scan it directly. The app automatically retrieves details like the title, author, and Dewey Decimal Classification numbers to build the Cutter number for you.
Metadata is provided by OpenLibrary, an open community database, so some records may occasionally be incomplete or inaccurate.
Metadata is provided by OpenLibrary (openlibrary.org). See the Credits section below.
Can I browse and search full Cutter tables directly?
Yes. Beyond generating numbers automatically, you can open the Cutter Table view to browse all entries arranged in alphabetical sections.
Can I customize how my cutter numbers look?
You can tailor your call numbers to match your library’s style:
• Custom Prefixes & Suffixes: Choose whether letters before or after the number come from the author\'s surname or the book title.
• Letter Count: Decide how many characters to include at the beginning or end.
• Smart Grammar Controls: Turn on settings to automatically ignore articles like \'The\', \'An\', or \'El\', or convert prefixes like \'Mc\' to \'Mac\'.
Can I save my work and export it later?

Yes, all your generated Cutter numbers are automatically saved. When you\'re finished processing your books, you can export your entire list into a CSV spreadsheet to load into your cataloging software.
Can I import my own custom Cutter table?
Yes. You can import custom Cutter tables by uploading a CSV (Comma-Separated Values) file.

Which Cutter tables are available in the app?
• PHA Table: Heloisa De Almeida Prado 1983 third edition.
• Old Spanish Alphabet Cutter: Traditional Spanish alphabet table including CH and LL letters.
You can switch between them at any time in the app settings or %s tab.

The csv file needs to follow the format "<name>","<number>" for example:"Zac","15". If the file has headers please set ON the option above.

Cutter App is a friendly, time-saving tool designed for librarians, catalogers, and book lovers to easily generate and manage Cutter call numbers. Instead of manually flipping through tables, the app quickly turns author names and book titles into accurate catalog numbers, helping you keep your library organized with minimal effort.
Cutter App is free and open source. You can inspect the source code, report issues, or contribute to its development.
